dimensions.assessment: Directly affects pharmaceutical companies, brand-name drug manufacturers submitting citizen petitions, and generic drug or biosimilar applicants.
dimensions.evidence: A person submitting or causing the submission of a covered petition or a series of covered petitions that is a sham shall be liable

dimensions.assessment: Subjects liable parties to substantial civil penalties, including revenue earned during the review period or up to $50,000 per day.
dimensions.evidence: any revenue earned from the sale... or $50,000 for each calendar day that each covered petition... was under review

dimensions.assessment: Imposes civil financial penalties and potential revenue forfeitures to the federal government, though exact aggregate fiscal totals are not stated.
Expands FTC enforcement powers to address specific categories of FDA petitions as unfair methods of competition under the Federal Trade Commission Act.
dimensions.evidence: enable the Federal Trade Commission to deter filing of sham citizen petitions... and for other purposes

dimensions.assessment: Provides ongoing regulatory and legal enforcement authority for petitions submitted on or after the date of enactment.
dimensions.evidence: This section shall apply to any covered petition submitted on or after the date of enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Estimates of how many citizen petitions will be challenged annually.
Projected administrative costs for the FTC and HHS to manage referrals and enforcement actions.
importance_detail.rationale: S. 1095 establishes FTC enforcement and civil penalties against sham citizen petitions submitted to the FDA regarding generic and biosimilar drug applications, affecting pharmaceutical companies and federal regulatory reviews.
